sentences: In the present day, an elderly man reads a romantic story from a notebook to a female patient in their nursing home.
The story opens in 1940 at a carnival in a town.
A lumber mill worker sees a 17-year-old heiress and immediately falls in love with her.
He pursues her, woos her into dating him, and they begin a romance.
The mill worker and the heiress fall head-over-heels in love despite their differences.
Near the end of the summer, the mill worker learns that the heiress will attend a college in another state in the fall.
He takes her to a plantation, telling her about his dream to repair its abandoned house.
They try to have sex, but things are a bit awkward since they both are not sure what to do and a nervous heiress can't stop talking.
They are interrupted by their friend who tells them that the heiress's parents have summoned the police to find her.
When the heiress and the mill worker return to her parents' mansion, the heiress's mother, who thinks the working-class mill worker is not good enough for the heiress, forbids her from seeing him.
The mill worker overhears the conversation and admits to the heiress he does not see a future for them.
A distraught heiress breaks up with him, but immediately regrets the decision.
The next morning, the mother announces they will be returning to the city immediately.
The heiress rushes to the lumber mill to apologize to the mill worker, but he is away; she asks their friend to tell him she loves him.
The mill worker rushes to the heiress's home when the message is delivered, but she has already left.
The mill worker writes to the heiress every day for a year, but the heiress's mother intercepts the letters.
When the country joins the war, the mill worker and their friend enlist and fight in a battle, where the friend is killed.
Meanwhile, the heiress nurses soldiers in a hospital, meeting a wounded captain, a young lawyer who comes from old southern money.
After a few years, they become engaged, to the heiress's parents' delight.
The mill worker returns from the war, to find his father has sold their home so the mill worker can buy the plantation.
Soon after, his father dies, and the mill worker begins repairing the house.
The mill worker cannot bring himself to sell the house since it connects him to the heiress.
Out of loneliness, the mill worker has a casual relationship with a war widow.
As the heiress tries on her wedding dress, she sees a newspaper photo of the mill worker in front of his renovated house and faints.
The heiress's feelings for the mill worker resurface, so she decides to travel to the town.
There, she comes face to face with the mill worker for the first time in seven years.
They have a pleasant afternoon catching up and the mill worker invites the heiress to come over again the next day.
After a romantic boat ride, the heiress emotionally confronts the mill worker about why he did not write to her all those years ago.
The mill worker tells her he did write to her and they kiss.
They go back to the house and have sex.
The heiress and the mill worker spend the next couple of days in romantic bliss.
The mother arrives to warn the heiress that the captain has come to the town.
She reveals that she once also loved a lower-class man and wonders what their lives would have been like had she chosen differently.
The mother gives the mill worker's letters to the heiress and suggests she choose wisely.
The heiress admits to the mill worker she does not know what to do and this leads to an explosive argument between the pair.
The mill worker tells the heiress she has to choose who she truly wants to be with.
The heiress drives back to her hotel and confesses her infidelity to the captain.
The captain forgives her and still wants to marry her.
Ultimately, the heiress follows her heart and returns to the mill worker.
Back in the present, the elderly woman is revealed to be the heiress, now suffering from dementia.
An eight-year-old boy idolizes a famed explorer, who is discredited when a giant bird skeleton he brought back from a waterfall in another country is deemed fake.
The explorer travels back to the falls, vowing not to return until he brings back a live specimen.

The boy befriends a girl, another young fan of the explorer, who keeps a scrapbook of her adventures and dreams of moving her "clubhouse" (an abandoned house) to the falls and having adventures of her own.
The boy and the girl eventually marry, renovate the clubhouse and move in, working at the city zoo as a balloon salesman and zookeeper, respectively.
The wife suffers a miscarriage, and they learn they cannot have children.
The couple saves money for a trip to the falls, but are repeatedly forced to spend their savings on more pressing needs.
Many years later, the now elderly husband decides to surprise his wife with tickets to the country, but she falls ill and is hospitalized, giving her husband her scrapbook before she dies.
Now in his late 70s, the old man holds out while the neighborhood around him is redeveloped.
After unintentionally injuring a construction worker who accidentally damaged his mailbox, the old man is ordered by a court to move into an assisted living facility.
However, the old man resolves to keep his promise to his wife to move their house to the falls and attaches numerous balloons to it in order to fly there.
A young scout attempting to earn his final merit badge for assisting the elderly becomes an accidental stowaway.
Before the old man can land and send the scout home, a storm propels the house all the way to a tepui in the country.
The old man and the scout harness themselves to the still-buoyant house and tow it across the mesa.

Along the way, they encounter a giant flightless bird that the scout gives a male name (though the bird is later revealed to be female) and a golden retriever whose collar has a device that translates his thoughts into human speech.
After failed attempts to evade the animals, the old man reluctantly allows both to join the party.
The retriever's pack, all wearing collar translators, surrounds them.
The dogs' master is revealed to be the elderly explorer, who invites the old man and the scout aboard his airship and discusses his quest to capture the bird.
However, the old man's initial excitement over meeting him fades as he realizes that the explorer's obsession has driven him insane.
After the explorer shows them the bird skeleton, the scout notes its resemblance to the bird.
Becoming hostile, the explorer reveals that he has murdered other travelers he suspected of also seeking the bird.
The old man, the scout and the retriever flee, pursued by the explorer's dogs; they are rescued by the bird, who gets injured in the process.
Hearing the bird call out to her chicks, the old man agrees to take her home.
However, the explorer captures her and starts a fire beneath the old man's home.
Forced to choose, the old man saves his home, allowing the explorer to take the bird away and losing the scout's respect.

Disheartened, the old man looks through his wife's scrapbook and discovers that she had filled in blank pages with photos of their life together and written "Thanks for the adventure – now go have a new one!".
Reinvigorated, he goes outside, only to see the scout flying after the bird using balloons and a leaf blower.
The old man lightens his house by emptying it completely, enabling it to fly again.
The scout arrives at the explorer's airship but is caught.
The old man and the retriever, the latter of whom stowed away, board the dirigible and free him and the bird.
The explorer pursues them and traps the scout, the bird, and the retriever inside the house, but the old man saves them just as the tether breaks.
The explorer leaps after them, but gets his leg tangled in balloon strings and falls to his death.
The old man's house, having lost several balloons, descends out of sight beneath the clouds.
The old man, the retriever, and the scout reunite the bird with her chicks before returning home to their own country in the explorer's airship.

The scout receives his badge for assisting the elderly, and the old man presents the scout with a bottle cap his wife gave the old man when they first met as kids years ago, which he dubs a badge named after her.
Meanwhile, unbeknownst to the old man, the tepui his house landed on overlooks the falls, fulfilling his promise to his wife.
A princess of a kingdom has naturally occurring magical powers, allowing her to create ice and snow.
After she accidentally injures her younger sister with her magic, their parents bring them to a colony of trolls led by a troll chief.
He heals the younger sister and erases her memories of the elder sister's magic.
The king and queen decide that until the elder sister learns to control her powers, they will close the castle gates and isolate her.
Years of isolation create a rift between the sisters and, when they are adolescents, their parents die in a shipwreck.
On the elder sister's coronation day, the castle gates open to the public for the first time.
Visiting dignitaries include the handsome prince of a foreign kingdom, with whom the younger sister falls in love at first sight.
The prince proposes to the younger sister, but the elder sister objects to the marriage and lashes out, accidentally revealing her powers to the terrified court.
Accused of witchcraft by the scheming duke, the elder sister flees to the mountain and feels free for the first time.
She builds an ice palace and decides to live a hermit's life, unaware that her magic has plunged the kingdom into an eternal winter.
The younger sister ventures out to find the elder sister, leaving the prince in command.
She meets an ice courier and his reindeer, and convinces them to bring her to the mountain.
On the way they meet a living snowman created by the elder sister's magic, who agrees to guide them.
At the ice palace, the younger sister tells the elder sister about what has become of the kingdom.
The elder sister's fear makes her accidentally hit the younger sister with ice again, freezing her heart.
Unknowing of this, the elder sister creates a giant snow monster in desperation and casts the younger sister out of the castle to keep her safe.
With the younger sister slowly freezing to death, the courier takes her to the trolls for help.
The troll chief says that only "an act of true love" can thaw her heart.
The courier and the snowman race the younger sister back to the castle so the prince can give her a true love's kiss.
Meanwhile, the prince defeats the giant snow monster and imprisons the elder sister, after a fight between her and the duke's bodyguards.

Instead of kissing the younger sister, the prince reveals that he has been plotting to become ruler of the kingdom by marrying her and then killing the elder sister, leaving the younger sister to freeze to death.
The sisters escape, and the snowman helps the younger sister reunite with the courier, whom he has inferred is in love with the younger sister.
The prince confronts the elder sister, saying that she has killed the younger sister.
The elder sister breaks down, which abruptly stops the extreme blizzard she recently created.
Seeing the prince about to kill the elder sister, the younger sister sacrifices her chance to be saved by the courier and steps between the elder sister and the prince.
She freezes solid, which devastates the elder sister.
As she hugs her sister, the younger sister slowly thaws; her heroism is "an act of true love".
Realizing that love is the key to controlling her powers, the elder sister ends the winter.
The prince is arrested and exiled for treason and attempted assassination.
The courier is appointed the royal ice deliverer, and he and the younger sister share a kiss.
The sisters mend their relationship, and the elder sister promises never to lock the castle gates again.
The space shuttle, commanded by a veteran astronaut, is in orbit around the planet to service a space telescope.
A doctor is aboard on her first space mission, to perform hardware upgrades on the telescope.

During a spacewalk, mission control on the ground warns the shuttle's crew about a rapidly expanding cloud of space debris caused by the Russians shooting down a defunct spy satellite, and orders the crew to return to the planet immediately.
Communication with mission control is lost shortly after, as more communication satellites are disabled by debris.
Debris strikes the shuttle and the telescope, tearing the doctor from the shuttle.
The commander, using a thruster pack, rescues her and they return to the shuttle, discovering that it has suffered catastrophic damage and the rest of the crew are dead.
The commander decides they should use the thruster pack to reach a space station, which is in orbit about 1,450 km (900 mi) away.
He estimates that they have 90 minutes before the debris field completes an orbit and threatens them again.
On their way to the station, the two discuss the doctor's home life and her daughter, who died young in an accident.
As they approach the station, they see that the station's crew has evacuated using one of its two spacecraft, with the remaining craft exhibiting damage and unable to return to the planet.
The commander suggests using it to travel to the nearby Chinese space station, 100 km (60 mi) away, to board its similar spacecraft and return to the planet.
They try to grab onto the station, but only make tenuous connection to the craft's parachute cords, which are not strong enough for them both.
Despite the doctor's protests, the commander detaches himself to save her from drifting away with him.
The doctor enters the station as the commander floats away.
Unable to establish communication with him, she concludes that she is the mission's sole survivor.
Inside the station, a fire breaks out, forcing the doctor to rush to the craft.
As she maneuvers it away from the station, the tangled parachute tethers snag, preventing the spacecraft from leaving.
She performs a spacewalk to cut the cables, succeeding just as the debris field returns, destroying the station.
The doctor angles the craft towards the Chinese station but discovers that the engine has no fuel.
After an attempt at radio communication with an Inuk on the planet, the doctor resigns herself to her fate and shuts off the cabin's oxygen supply to commit suicide.
As she begins to lose consciousness, she experiences a hallucination of the commander telling her to rig the craft's soft landing rockets to propel the capsule towards the Chinese station.
The doctor regains the will to go on, restoring the spacecraft's oxygen flow and rigging the landing rockets accordingly.
Unable to dock with the Chinese station, the doctor ejects herself from the craft and uses a fire extinguisher as a makeshift thruster to travel to the rapidly deorbiting station.
She enters the Chinese station's capsule just as the station enters the upper atmosphere, and undocks.
The capsule re-enters the atmosphere and lands in a lake.
Radio communication from mission control informs the doctor that she has been tracked on radar and that rescue crews are on their way.
The doctor opens the hatch and sheds her space suit, allowing her to reach the surface and crawl onto the beach before standing and walking away.
In 2035, the crew of a mission to another planet is exploring a region on local solar day (sol) 18 of their 31-sol expedition.
A severe dust storm threatens their ascent vehicle and in the ensuing evacuation, one astronaut is struck by flying debris and presumed dead.
Facing imminent peril, the remaining crew takes off for their orbiting vessel, which will then return them to the home planet.
The astronaut awakens after the storm, having narrowly survived his injuries.
As he recovers within the crew's surface habitat, he begins a video diary to document his thoughts on survival.
Unable to communicate with the home planet, his only chance of rescue is the next mission to the planet in four years, when that mission will land at a crater.
The next mission's ascent vehicle has already arrived on the site in preparation for the mission.
With this timeframe in mind, the astronaut's main survival concerns are food and travel.
Being a botanist, he cultivates a potato garden inside the habitat using the crew's bio-waste with the planet's soil, and creates water from leftover rocket fuel.
He also modifies a rover for the journey to the crater.
On the home planet, a space agency satellite planner notices the astronaut's activity from recorded satellite images, and suspects he must be alive.
The space agency's director releases the news to the public but decides not to inform the crew en route to the home planet, over the flight director's strong objection.
The astronaut explores the surrounding terrain and studies his maps, but he quickly journeys out to retrieve a probe, hoping to restore its communications.
The missions director realizes this strategy, and quickly visits a laboratory director to use their replica of the probe.
The agency makes contact with the astronaut and instructs him to link the probe to the rover, where he can now communicate by text.
With this breakthrough, the flight director is finally allowed to inform the astronaut's crewmates.
As the astronaut enters the habitat on one evening, a leak in the airlock causes an explosion that injures him and destroys the potato garden.
Although he repairs the airlock, he is again threatened by starvation.
The space agency scrambles to procure a resupply ship for the astronaut, with the agency director ordering routine safety inspections bypassed to expedite the mission.
This oversight results in catastrophe as the ship disintegrates shortly after launch.
The Chinese space agency decides to offer a launch vehicle – originally intended for a space probe – to resupply the astronaut.

An astrodynamicist devises an alternative plan: send that launcher to resupply the vessel, which will then use the home planet's gravity to "slingshot" back to the planet two years earlier than the next mission.
The agency director flatly rejects the idea, considering it too risky for the crew.
The flight director surreptitiously sends the proposal to the crew, and they unanimously vote in favor and divert the vessel.
The agency director is forced to support them publicly, but demands the flight director's resignation after the mission.
After waiting several months, the astronaut embarks on the long journey to the next mission's ascent vehicle.
He plans to use it to rendezvous with the vessel, but needs to lighten the load considerably by partially dismantling the cockpit.
He takes off to orbit, but the vessel's crew find that they remain too far away and moving too fast to retrieve him.
The commander quickly improvises to explode the airlock in part of the ship, resulting in air violently escaping and slowing them down.
The commander also pilots a tethered thruster pack to personally reach the astronaut, but they are still too far apart.
The astronaut quickly improvises by piercing his pressure suit, and propels himself with the escaping air, reaches the commander, and manages to hold on.
The space agency and spectators across the world all celebrate the successful rescue.
After returning to the home planet, the astronaut becomes a survival instructor for astronaut candidates.
Five years later, as a later mission is launching, those involved in the astronaut's rescue are seen in their current lives watching the launch footage.

The commercial space tug is returning home with a seven-member crew in stasis: the captain, the executive officer, the warrant officer, the navigator, the science officer, and two engineers, along with the ship's cat.
The ship's computer detects a transmission from a nearby exomoon and wakes the crew.
Following company policy to investigate transmissions indicating intelligent life, they leave their payload in orbit and land on the surface, but the ship is damaged.
The captain, the executive officer, and the navigator discover that the transmission comes from a derelict alien vessel.
Inside is a giant, fossilized alien corpse with a hole in its torso.
Meanwhile, the computer partially deciphers the transmission, which the warrant officer determines is a warning beacon and not an SOS as initially thought.
The executive officer enters a chamber containing hundreds of large eggs.
When he touches one, an arthropod-like life form springs out, penetrates his helmet, and attaches to his face.
Back at the ship, the warrant officer refuses to allow them aboard, citing quarantine regulations, but the science officer disobeys her.

While the engineers work on ship repairs, the science officer attempts to extricate the creature from the executive officer's face but stops when he discovers that its highly corrosive acidic blood could harm the executive officer and damage the ship's hull.
The creature eventually detaches itself and dies.
After the crew returns to space, the executive officer awakens and seems well.
During a final crew meal before returning to stasis, he suddenly chokes and convulses as a small alien creature bursts from his chest and escapes into the ship.
After ejecting the executive officer's body into space, the crew uses tracking devices to try to locate and kill the creature.
Encountering the cat, one engineer follows him into a landing leg compartment, where the now fully-grown alien kills him.
The crew determines that the alien is moving around the ship within the air ducts, and the captain devises a plan to force the creature off the ship with an airlock.
The captain asks the computer about alternative methods of killing the alien and their chances of succeeding, but the computer refuses to answer.
He then enters the ducts with a flamethrower but is ambushed and killed by the alien.
A panic-stricken navigator suggests abandoning the ship and leaving in the ship's escape shuttle.
The warrant officer, now in command, rejects the plan because the shuttle cannot support the remaining four crew members and decides that they will reattempt the captain's plan.
She accesses the computer herself and discovers a secret company directive: the science officer must return with the alien for study, regardless of risk to the crew.
The science officer attempts to kill her when confronted, but the other engineer arrives and incapacitates the science officer, who is revealed to be an android.
Upon interrogation, the science officer admires the alien and claims that the crew stands no chance against it.
The other engineer incinerates the science officer's remains.
Hearing this, the warrant officer decides to proceed with the navigator's plan and initiate the ship's self-destruct mechanism.
While they are gathering supplies, the alien kills the other engineer and the navigator.
Now alone, the warrant officer begins the self-destruction, but the alien blocks her route to the escape shuttle.
She narrowly escapes and turns back to abort the sequence but fails to return before the override option expires.
With only five minutes left to evacuate, the warrant officer frantically returns to the shuttle and finds that the alien is gone.
She takes the cat, boards the shuttle and launches it seconds before the ship explodes.
As the warrant officer prepares for stasis, she discovers that the alien has stowed itself in a narrow compartment aboard the shuttle.
She dons a spacesuit, loads a grappling hook gun, and straps herself to a chair before discharging gases to drive the alien from its hiding place.
It tries to attack her, but she opens the shuttle door.
The resulting depressurization blast leaves the alien clinging to the door frame.
The warrant officer shoots it with the gun, knocking it out, but the door closes on the grapple line, leaving the alien tethered to the ship.
She then fires the engines to sever the line and blast the alien into space.
After recording her log entry, she places the cat and herself into stasis to start their return journey home.
To mark the country's upcoming bicentennial, the heavyweight boxing world champion plans to hold a title bout in the city.
However, he is informed five weeks from the fight date that his scheduled opponent is unable to compete due to an injured hand.
All other potential replacements are either booked or unable to get into shape in time.
Having invested heavily into the fight, the champion decides to give a local contender a chance to challenge him.
He selects an Italian-American journeyman southpaw boxer living in poverty, who primarily fights in small gyms and works as a collector for a mob loan shark.
The challenger is chosen on the basis of his nickname, because the champion feels that the name is most suitable for marketing purposes.
The challenger meets with a promoter and agrees to the fight, which will pay him $150,000.
The challenger puts himself through several weeks of unorthodox and improvised training, such as using sides of beef as punching bags.
He is later approached by a former bantamweight fighter-turned-trainer whose gym the challenger frequents, about further training.
The challenger is not willing initially, as the trainer has not shown much interest in helping him before and saw him as a wasted talent, but eventually he accepts the offer.
The challenger builds a romantic relationship with a shy woman who is working part-time at a pet store.
The woman's brother and the challenger's best friend sets his sister up on a date with the challenger.
She initially rejects his advances but consents to each subsequent step of the date when he continues to ask.
The brother also offers to work as a cornerman with him for the fight, an offer the challenger turns down.
The brother becomes jealous of the challenger's success, but the challenger placates him by agreeing to advertise the meat packing business where the brother works as part of the fight.
The challenger trains extensively for the match, while the champion is unconcerned and puts more effort into promotion than training.
The night before the match, the challenger visits the arena and begins to lose confidence.
He confesses to the woman that he does not believe he can win but strives to go the distance against the champion, which no other fighter has done, to prove himself.
On the first day of the new year, the fight is held with the champion making a dramatic entrance dressed as one national icon and then another.
Taking advantage of his overconfidence, the challenger knocks him down in the first round—the first time that the champion has ever been knocked down.

Humbled and worried, the champion takes the challenger more seriously for the rest of the fight, which goes on for the full fifteen rounds, with both combatants sustaining various injuries: the challenger, with hits to the head and swollen eyes, requires his right eyelid to be cut to restore his vision, while the champion, with internal bleeding and a broken rib, struggles to breathe.
As the fight concludes, the champion's skill is countered by the challenger's stamina, toughness and will.
As the final bell sounds, the champion tells the challenger there "ain't gonna be no rematch".
The challenger replies that he does not want one.
As the ring is flooded with reporters and excited fans, the challenger calls out repeatedly for the woman, who makes her way into the ring.
As the promoter declares the champion the winner by virtue of a split decision, the challenger and the woman embrace and profess their love for each other, unconcerned with the outcome of the fight.
The family is preparing to spend the holidays in a foreign city, gathering at the parents' home in a suburb the night before their departure.
Their youngest son is the subject of ridicule by his older siblings because of his immaturity.
During a scuffle with his oldest brother, the boy accidentally ruins the family dinner; while cleaning up the mess, the father inadvertently throws away the boy's flight ticket.
As punishment, the mother sends the boy to the attic, where he angrily berates his mother and wishes his family would disappear.
During the night, heavy winds cause a power outage that resets the alarm clocks and leads the family to oversleep.
The next morning, in the chaotic rush to leave for the airport, the boy is accidentally left behind.
The boy wakes to find the house empty and, thinking that his wish has come true, initially enjoys his newfound freedom.
He ransacks his oldest brother's room, buys and eats whatever he wants, and watches violent movies.

However, the boy soon becomes frightened by his next door neighbor, an old man, who is rumored by his oldest brother to be a serial killer who murdered his own family in the 1950's, as well as a pair of burglars who have been breaking into other vacant houses in the neighborhood and have targeted the family's house.
The boy tricks them into thinking that his family is still home, forcing them to put their plans on hold.
The mother realizes mid-flight that the boy was left behind.
Upon arrival in the foreign city, the family discovers that all flights for the next two days are fully booked.
While the rest of the family stay in the father's brother's apartment, the mother manages to get a flight to their home country, but it is a flight to a different city.
On the eve of the holiday, the mother ends up in yet another city, where all flights to her home city are fully booked.
She ends up riding with a polka band who are driving to another city and whose leader offered to let her ride with them to her home city after overhearing her desperation to get home.
Meanwhile, the burglars finally realize that the boy is home alone, and the boy overhears them discussing plans to break into his house.
The boy starts to miss his family and asks the local holiday gift-bringer impersonator if he could bring them back for the holidays.
He goes to a church and watches a choir perform, then meets the old man, who dispels the rumors about him.
He points out his granddaughter in the choir, whom he is unable to spend the holidays with, as he and his son are estranged; the boy suggests that he should reconcile with his son.
The boy returns home and rigs the house with booby traps to take on the burglars.
The burglars break in, spring the traps, and suffer various injuries.
While the duo pursues the boy around the house, he calls the police and flees, then lures the burglars into a neighboring home which they previously broke into.
They catch him and prepare to get their revenge, but the old man, who is next door checking on his son's house, intervenes and knocks them unconscious with his snow shovel.
The police arrive and arrest the burglars, having identified all the houses that they broke into due to one burglar's destructive characteristic of flooding them.
On the holiday morning, the boy is disappointed to find that his family is still gone.

He then hears the mother enter the house and call for him; they reconcile and are soon joined by the father, the oldest brother, and three other family members, who managed to return by catching a flight to that same city and then a connecting flight to their home city.
The boy keeps silent about his encounter with the burglars, although the father finds the other burglar's knocked-out gold tooth.
The boy then observes the old man reuniting with his son, daughter-in-law, and granddaughter.
The old man notices the boy, and the pair wave to each other knowingly.
The film ends with the boy getting into trouble when his oldest brother discovers the mess in his room which the boy went into earlier.
A young anthropomorphic rat with heightened senses of taste and smell dreams of becoming a chef like his human idol, a late chef.
Conversely, the rest of his colony, including his older brother and their father, the clan leader, only eat for sustenance and are wary of humans.
The rats live in an elderly woman's attic outside the city, but when the woman discovers them, the young rat becomes separated from the others during their hasty evacuation.
Encouraged by an imaginary version of the late chef, he explores until he finds himself on the roof of the late chef's namesake restaurant.
The young rat sees the restaurant's new garbage boy struggling to fix a leek soup he ruined.

The young rat sneaks in and improves the soup; the garbage boy notices and traps the young rat while keeping his presence secret from the late chef's former sous-chef and the restaurant's new owner and head chef.
The sous-chef confronts the garbage boy about the soup, but it is served by accident and unexpectedly becomes a hit.
The restaurant's only female chef persuades the sous-chef to keep the garbage boy and support the late chef's motto, "Anyone can cook."
The sous-chef demands the garbage boy replicate the soup but spots the young rat, ordering the garbage boy to take him outside and kill him.
Alone, the garbage boy realizes the young rat understands him and persuades the young rat to assist with cooking.
The young rat discovers that he can control the garbage boy's movements like a marionette by pulling on his hair while hiding under his toque.
They recreate the soup and continue cooking at the restaurant.
The female chef begrudgingly trains the garbage boy but steadily appreciates him heeding her advice.
Later, the young rat reunites with his clan.

After the young rat tells the father that he intends to stay at the restaurant, the father shows him a group of exterminated rats to convince him that humans are dangerous, but the young rat defies his warnings and leaves.

Meanwhile, the sous-chef is shocked and enraged to discover through a letter from the garbage boy's late mother that the late chef is the garbage boy's father, making him the rightful owner of the restaurant.
After the sous-chef's lawyer verifies that the garbage boy is the late chef's son, the sous-chef hides the evidence in an envelope; the young rat steals the envelope and brings it to the garbage boy.
The sous-chef is fired and the garbage boy is promoted to head chef.
The restaurant thrives as the young rat's recipes become popular, and the garbage boy develops a romantic relationship with the female chef.
A food critic, who negatively reviewed the restaurant shortly before the late chef's death, announces to the garbage boy that he will review the restaurant again the following day.
After the garbage boy takes credit for the young rat's cooking at a press conference, he and the young rat have a falling out.
As revenge, the young rat leads his clan on a raid of the restaurant's pantries.
The garbage boy arrives to apologize, but upon discovering the raid, he furiously expels the young rat and his clan from the restaurant.
The next day, the sous-chef captures the young rat, who is quickly freed by the father and the brother.
After returning to the restaurant, he and the garbage boy reconcile, and the garbage boy reveals the young rat and his cooking techniques to his staff, who all immediately quit.
The father, impressed by the young rat's grit, summons the clan to help him cook while the garbage boy waits tables.
Reminded of the late chef's motto, the female chef returns to help.
The sous-chef and a health inspector attempt to interfere, but the rats tie them up, gag them and lock them in the pantry.
The young rat prepares confit byaldi, a variation of ratatouille, which evokes in the critic a sudden and involuntary recollection of his childhood and of his mother's cooking.
Astonished and delighted, the critic asks to meet the chef and – once all other guests are gone – is stunned when introduced to the young rat.
The next day, he writes a glowing review, stating that he has come to understand the late chef's motto and praising the young rat without revealing that he is a rat.
After the sous-chef and the health inspector are released and expose the rat infestation, the restaurant is shut down, costing the critic his job and reputation.
The young rat, the garbage boy, and the female chef open a bistro, which a now-happier critic invests in and frequents.
The rat colony settles into the bistro's attic as their new home.

On a fictional Greek island (whose name is Greek for 'summer'), a bride-to-be reveals to her bridesmaids that she has secretly invited three men to her wedding without telling her mother: an Irish-American architect, a Swedish travel writer, and a British banker.

One of the three is the bride's biological father, though she doesn't know which, and she wants him to give her away at the wedding; she believes that after spending time with each of them, she will learn who fathered her.
When the three men arrive at the island, the bride explains she sent the wedding invitations, not the mother, but does not reveal that she believes one of them is her father.
She hides the men in the mother's goat house, and they hesitantly agree not to reveal themselves yet, as it is a surprise.
As the mother is working on the goat house, she spies on them.
Dumbfounded to find herself facing her former lovers, she demands they leave.
The mother confides in her two old friends, who have also arrived for the wedding, that she truly does not know which of the three fathered the bride.
The bride finds the men aboard the writer's sailboat and they sail around the island, with the men bonding with the bride and telling her stories of the mother's carefree youth.
The bride attempts to tell her fiancé about her ploy but loses her nerve.
At the bride's bachelorette party, the mother is distressed by the three men's presence, but her two friends assure her that they will take care of them.
The bride talks with each man alone.

The writer learns that the mother received the money for her villa from his great-aunt whereas he had understood the money was bequeathed "to family"; as a result, they believe he is her father and she asks him to give her away but keep their secret until the wedding.
The architect deduces (rightly or wrongly) that he is her father and asks who is giving her away.
She says "no-one" and the architect offers.
They agree to keep it a secret until the wedding.
The banker similarly deduces (rightly or wrongly) and states that he'll walk her down the aisle, giving her no chance to decline.
In the morning, the mother attempts to comfort the bride and offers to cancel the wedding; the bride reacts angrily, saying she wants to avoid her mother's mistakes.
The architect attempts to discuss the wedding with the mother, and both realize they still have feelings for each other.
The bride admits her actions to her fiancé and asks for his help, but he reacts angrily to her deception.
As they prepare for the wedding the mother admits to the bride that her mother disowned her after she got pregnant, but she could not be more proud of having her.
The bride then asks the mother to give her away, to which the mother happily agrees.
As the bridal party and guests enter the chapel the architect intercepts the mother, who reveals the pain she felt over losing him.
At the wedding, the architect reveals that he had ended his engagement, but returned to find the mother had gone off with another man (the writer).
The three men agree with the bride that they do not want the paternity confirmed, each agreeing to be one-third of a father for the bride.
The bride suggests to her fiancé that they postpone their wedding and travel the world.
The architect proposes to the mother, revealing that he is divorced and has always loved her.
She happily accepts and they marry on the spot.
